answer.text: each of them understood a different person to be in charge of the DNA work
answer.line: Wilkins seems to have expected an assistant. Franklin read Randall's letter as making the problem hers. Two readings of one job.

steps: Find Franklin's arrival: paragraph 5. The friction sits in sentence 5.
Read both halves of that sentence. Wilkins seems to have expected an assistant; she understood the problem was now hers.
Sentence 6 closes it: the misunderstanding was never repaired. Two people, two readings.

choices.text: Randall had removed Wilkins from the biophysics unit before Franklin arrived
choices.note: Nothing removes Wilkins: paragraph 5 calls him Randall's deputy, and in paragraph 9 he is still there to show Watson Photo 51.

choices.text: each of them understood a different person to be in charge of the DNA work
choices.note: Paragraph 5, sentence 5: his assistant, in his reading; her problem, in hers.

choices.text: Franklin refused to share Gosling's earlier photographs with Wilkins
choices.note: No refusal to share photographs appears anywhere. It sounds like a reason for friction, which is the pull.

choices.text: Wilkins had been trained in Paris and distrusted her Cambridge methods
choices.note: Cambridge and Paris are Franklin's own training, paragraph 5, sentence 4. The choice pins her background on Wilkins.

choices.text: Franklin had publicly criticized the quality of Wilkins's diffraction patterns
choices.note: Franklin criticizes the Cambridge model in paragraph 8, never Wilkins's patterns.
